meta.title: Introducing Slipr
meta.subtitle: One show, two ways to experience it
meta.author: Lucas Jellema
meta.description: A tour of Slipr (SlidePresenter): how one show serves both a live audience and an individual reader. This demo exercises every feature of the show format.

reveal-js.definition: Open-source framework for HTML presentations. Slipr uses it for **audience mode** only.

audience-layer.definition: The slide itself: concise content placed in the slots of a layout. Shown on the big screen.

reader-layer.definition: Extra, interactive content attached to a slide: panels, callouts, tabs, hotspots, embeds. Shown only in reader mode.

template.definition: A style guide (colors, fonts, illustrations) plus a set of base slide layouts. Every show links to one.

layout.definition: A base slide format in a template, such as *title*, *bullets* or *two-column*. It defines named slots.

slot.definition: A named place in a layout that a slide fills with content, e.g. `title` or `body`.

new-term.definition: The collection of slides and reader notes that make up a Slipr project

json.definition: JSON is JavaScript Object Notation, a compact dataformat.

content.title: Introducing Slipr
content.subtitle: One show, two ways to experience it

slides.notes: Welcome everyone. Promise a live switch between the two modes at the end.

reader.summary: Slipr turns one source into a live slideshow and an interactive reading experience.

blocks.md: Welcome! You are reading the **reader version** of a presentation. Hover or tap the underlined terms, open the [[template|panels]], and use the controls to choose how deep you want to go.

content.title: Why another presentation tool?
content.body:
- Slides are made for the **room**
- Afterwards they are **read alone**
  - without the speaker's story
- Two documents drift apart

slides.notes: Ask the audience: who has ever received a deck afterwards that made no sense without the talk?

reader.summary: Decks are written for the room and fall flat when read alone.

blocks.md: A good talk keeps its slides sparse: the speaker carries the story. But the deck is what people keep, share and read later^[Think of how often you open a deck after a talk, compared to how long you watched it during the talk.], and on its own it rarely makes sense.
Slipr gives every slide two layers. The [[audience-layer]] stays concise for the big screen, rendered with [[reveal-js]]. The [[reader-layer]] adds depth for whoever reads it later.

blocks.title: Isn't this what PowerPoint notes pages are for?
blocks.md: Notes pages are the closest thing, but they are static, printed below a thumbnail, and not tailored to anyone. Slipr's reader layer is interactive, can be filtered by profile and depth, and is searchable.

blocks.title: The business case
blocks.md: One source instead of a deck *plus* a whitepaper: less work, and the two can never contradict each other.

content.title: One show, two experiences
content.left:
- Linear, presenter-driven
- Animations and builds
- High-level overviews
- Speaker notes and timer
content.right:
- Explore at your own pace
- Popups, panels, tabs
- Tailored to who you are
- Search, bookmarks, notes

slides.notes: This is the core idea. Pause here.

reader.summary: Audience mode is a slideshow; reader mode is an interactive, personal experience.

image.alt: A big screen in front of an audience, and a single reader at a laptop

blocks.md: The two modes are deliberately **separate applications**. Audience mode is a thin layer over [[reveal-js]]. Reader mode is built from scratch, because popups, tailored content and annotations need full control. See [the architecture](#s-architecture).

content.title: A show is just data
content.body:
- `show.json` + `images/`
- Linked to a template
- Slides name a **layout** and fill its **slots**
- No styling in the show, ever

image.alt: A JSON file: curly braces on a document

reader.summary: Shows are plain JSON; the template owns the looks.

blocks.md: Swap the [[template]] and the whole show is restyled, without touching a single slide.
Because content and looks are separated, a house style is enforced automatically, and shows are easy to keep under version control.

content.title: Three components, one shared core

image.alt: Slipr architecture: converter, show folder, editor, viewer, template and shared core

content.caption: The converter and editor produce shows; the viewer presents them.

slides.notes: Point at each box. Mention the converter is Python, the rest is vanilla JS.

reader.summary: Converter, editor and viewer share one data format and one renderer.

image.alt: Slipr architecture diagram with clickable components

blocks.caption: Click the markers to learn about each part.

hotspots.title: Converter
hotspots.md: Turns a `.pptx` into a show folder. Written in Python with `python-pptx`.

hotspots.title: Show folder
hotspots.md: `show.json` plus `images/`. Plain files: easy to inspect, diff and back up.

hotspots.title: Editor
hotspots.md: Browser app that edits both layers of a show, with a live preview.

hotspots.title: Viewer
hotspots.md: Two apps behind one URL: audience mode (Reveal.js) and reader mode.

hotspots.title: Template
hotspots.md: Style guide plus [[layout]]s. Owns every visual decision.

hotspots.title: Shared core
hotspots.md: Loading, validation and rendering, used by editor and viewer, so what you edit is what you present.

blocks.title: Technology choices
blocks.md: Vanilla HTML, CSS and ES modules: no build step and no framework. Third-party code is vendored so shows present offline. The JSON Schema in `shared/schema/` is the contract between the Python converter and the JavaScript apps.

blocks.md: Slipr supports **Mermaid diagrams** natively in both audience and reader mode. Diagrams are written as plain text in `show.json` and rendered directly in the browser into lightweight, scalable SVGs using vendored Mermaid.

content.caption: Web pages can be live and clickable while presenting, or shown as a screenshot.

reader.summary: Slides can hold a live web page.

blocks.md: A **web page** slot shows a page from the show folder or the web. While presenting it is live, or the author's screenshot. In reader mode, a page from another site waits for your click on **Load**.

content.title: A PDF, page by page
content.caption: Each click shows the next page.

reader.summary: Slides and the reader layer can show PDF documents.

blocks.md: A **PDF** slot shows one page, or steps through a range of pages on clicks. In reader mode, a PDF block has page navigation and zoom, and the PDF's text turns up in search.

reader.summary: Slides can hold an interactive map.

blocks.md: A **map** shows places with pins in the template's colors. While presenting it tours from place to place. In reader mode you pan, zoom and click a pin; the map tiles come from OpenStreetMap and load after your click on **Load**.

blocks.title: The route, fully offline

content.title: A table that tells a story
content.caption: Rows appear click by click, then a column and a row are highlighted. Click a header to sort.

reader.summary: Slides and reader blocks can hold data tables.

blocks.md: A **table** comes from a CSV file or is typed in. It takes its colours from the template, scrolls when it is long or wide, and can sort, filter and add up a column. While presenting, rows can appear one by one and a row, a column or a cell can be highlighted.

blocks.title: Sales per region (from a CSV file)
blocks.caption: Semicolons and decimal commas, as Excel writes them in Dutch. Country and Note are hidden: show them with Columns.

content.title: What a show is made of
content.caption: The bigger the word, the more the show is about it. In reader mode, click a word.

reader.summary: Slides and reader blocks can hold tag clouds.

blocks.md: A **tag cloud** sizes each term by its weight and colours it from the template. Terms come from a CSV file or are typed in; a term that names a glossary entry links to its definition. In reader mode a click shows the slides that mention the term; while presenting, the heaviest terms can appear first and terms can be highlighted.

blocks.title: What readers would use Slipr for (from a CSV file)
blocks.caption: One answer per row: repeated answers add up.

content.title: Bar charts that breathe life into numbers

chart.caption: Audience mode reveals bars step by step; reader mode adds exact tooltips, legend toggles and a switch to table view.

reader.summary: Bar charts can be placed in slides or as reader blocks.

blocks.md: A **bar chart** (`chart` slot or block) turns numbers into responsive SVG. It supports vertical and horizontal bars, grouped and stacked layouts, value labels, reference lines, and audience reveal steps.

content.title: Tailored to every reader
content.body:
- **Profiles**: content for who you are
- **Depth**: overview, standard, deep dive
- **Paths**: curated routes
- Search, bookmarks and your own notes

reader.summary: Profiles, depth and paths adapt the reader experience.

blocks.md: Every reader block can be aimed at specific profiles and given a depth. Pick a profile and a detail level in the toolbar, and the page adapts without losing your place.

blocks.title: Your data stays with you
blocks.md: Your choices, progress, bookmarks and notes are stored only in your own browser. Nothing is sent anywhere.

blocks.title: How filtering works
blocks.md: A pure function takes the show and your preferences and returns the visible slides and blocks: path selection first, then `reader.hidden`, then `for` (profile) and `depth ≤ level`.

content.title: Roadmap
content.left:
- Foundations: formats, template, this demo
- Audience mode
content.right:
- Reader core and personalisation
- PPTX converter
- Editor

reader.summary: Formats first, then both viewer modes, then converter and editor.

blocks.md: Each phase ends with something you can run and look at. The viewer comes first because it *is* the product; until the editor exists, shows like this one are written by hand with schema-driven autocomplete.

content.title: AI help, kept in its cage

image.alt: Illustration of a humanoid robot standing inside a birdcage, surrounded by floating documents and streams of data

content.caption: An assistant that answers only from the show's own content

slides.notes: Idea, not built yet. Emphasise: opt-in, and it never invents content beyond the show.

reader.summary: A future assistant that helps readers and authors, but only within the show's content.

blocks.md: Two ideas on the backlog use Claude: readers can **ask the show** a question, and authors get help drafting slides and writing a [[reader-layer]] from their speaker notes.

blocks.title: Why the cage?
blocks.md: The assistant only sees the show itself. It answers from that content, says so when the show has no answer, and never makes things up beyond it.
It is strictly opt-in: without an API key configured, Slipr works exactly as before and no data leaves the browser.

blocks.title: How would it work?
blocks.md: The show's text (slides, reader blocks, glossary) is the only context sent along with the question, and the answer cites the slide ids it used, so reader mode can link straight to them.

content.title: Backup: the show format
content.body:
- `chapters`, `glossary`, `profiles`, `paths`
- Per slide: `content` and `reader`
- Reader blocks: text, details, callout, tabs, image, embed, slide-ref
- Validated by a JSON Schema
